security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU TCG translates an instruction that straddles a page boundary between a tagcheck-exempt code page (MTAG=1, X=1) and a normal code page (MTAG=0 or no X), but does not apply the spec rule that the instruction is 'assumed to be fetched from normal code page' — causing loads/stores issued by that instruction to incorrectly bypass tag checks when they should be checked, or QEMU's page table walker in get_physical_address() fails to check the execute permission bit alongside the MTAG bit when classifying a page as 'tagged-data page' (requiring MTAG=1 AND X=0), causing code pages with MTAG=1 to be misclassified as tagged-data pages.
security_spec.summary: Cross-page instruction straddling between tagcheck-exempt and normal code pages must force unchecked-access treatment to the safer normal-page path, and tagged-data page classification must require execute=0 — failure in either causes guest memory-tagging bypass or spurious tag faults

findings.finding: hstatus CSR bit definitions (HSTATUS_VSBE through HSTATUS_HUPMM) exist and are correct for the implemented feature set. No HSTATUS_MTAG_I is defined because the src/mte_tag extension is not implemented in this QEMU tree. The WPRI masks at lines 685-686 correctly mark all unimplemented bits as read-as-zero/write-ignored, which includes whatever bit position MTAG_I would occupy. No violation of currently-implemented spec rules.

PTE bit definitions (PTE_V through PTE_ATTR) are correct for the implemented feature set. No PTE_MTAG is defined because the extension is not implemented. The PTE_RESERVED macro correctly treats bits 62-58 (or 63-58 depending on svrsw60t59b) as reserved, triggering TRANSLATE_FAIL if set. Any bit position that MTAG would use is correctly treated as reserved and causes a page fault. No misclassification of code vs. data pages based on MTAG can occur because MTAG is not read from PTEs.

Reserved-bit checking in the page table walker correctly rejects PTEs with reserved bits set via PTE_RESERVED(). Since no PTE_MTAG bit is defined, any PTE with the MTAG bit position set will trigger TRANSLATE_FAIL (page fault), which is the safe default behavior — no page can be incorrectly classified as tagged-data or tagcheck-exempt. PTE leaf classification at line 1466 uses only (PTE_R | PTE_W | PTE_X), which is correct for the implemented spec subset.

Leaf PTE protection-bit computation correctly derives PAGE_READ/PAGE_WRITE/PAGE_EXEC from PTE_R/PTE_W/PTE_X. No MTAG extraction occurs because the extension is unimplemented. The 'tagged-data page' classification (requiring MTAG=1 AND X=0 per the security spec) is not performed, which is correct — without the MTAG feature, all pages are treated uniformly with no tag-check bypass risk. MXR handling for execute-only pages is correctly implemented.

TLB fill correctly handles both two-stage (HLV/HSV) and single-stage translation paths. VS-stage translation followed by G-stage followed by PMP is architecturally correct. No tag-check hook exists between stages because the MTAG feature is unimplemented. The prot bitmask correctly flows from VS-stage through G-stage via prot &= prot2 (line 1873), and PMP via prot &= prot_pmp (line 1885). Adding a tag-check gate would be an extension, not a bug fix.

Central HLV/HSV permission check correctly enforces: M-mode bypass, virtual-instruction-fault when V=1, illegal-instruction for U-mode without HU. Returns (SPVP mode | MMU_2STAGE_BIT) with optional SUM promotion for S-mode stores. No MTAG_I check exists because the MTAG extension is not implemented. The function is architecturally correct for the current spec subset — there is no missing MTAG_I suppression because MTAG_I doesn't exist as a defined CSR field.

HLVX (hypervisor execute-load) helpers use cpu_ld*_code_mmu() which enforces execute permission via the MMU access type. The TODO comment at lines 710-714 correctly notes a known limitation (PMP should check read AND execute, currently only checks execute). This is unrelated to MTAG. No VMTAG_FETCH or MTAG_I interaction exists because the extension is not implemented. The current behavior is correct for the implemented spec.

TCG instruction translation dispatcher at line 1382. No page-boundary straddling detection exists for RISC-V (unlike target/arm/ and target/tricore/ which have insn_crosses_page()). Compressed instructions (RVC) can straddle page boundaries, but without MTAG implementation, there is no tagcheck-exempt vs. normal page distinction to violate. The existing page-fault behavior on the second half of a straddling RVC instruction is architecturally correct — it will fault if the second page is not executable, which is the safe default.

hstatus write handler correctly masks HUKTE and HUPMM conditionally on extension presence. All other writable bits are handled via the VPRI (WARL) pattern. No MTAG_I field exists to handle, so no masking is missing. The function is correct for the currently implemented CSR fields.

IOMMU device context validation: disallows MSI page tables (MSIPTP mode != OFF) when G-stage translation is BARE. This is a correctness fix for IOMMU configuration validation per the RISC-V IOMMU spec — when there is no second-stage translation, MSI address translation via page tables is invalid. This is unrelated to memory tagging (MTE/MTAG); the IOMMU 'tag' concept refers to translation-mode tags (bypass/single-stage/G-stage/nested), not memory tags.

VM live-migration state correctly serializes hstatus via VMSTATE_UINT64. No additional MTAG-related migration fields are needed because the MTAG extension is unimplemented. If MTAG_I were added as a separate architectural state field, a new VMSTATE entry and version bump would be required, but for the current code this is not a bug.

HLV/HSV/HLVX TCG translation correctly loads the source address from rs1, calls gen_helper_hyp_hlv/hsv, and stores the result to rd. No pre-processing (e.g., loading MTAG_I into a TCG temp for tag-suppression gating) is needed because the MTAG extension is unimplemented. The existing straightforward translation pattern is architecturally correct.

MMU index constants and accessor functions are correct for distinguishing U/S/M privilege modes, SUM override, and two-stage (HLV/HSV) lookups. HLV/HSV is disambiguated via MMU_2STAGE_BIT. No additional tag-checked vs. tag-unchecked mmu_idx bit is needed because the MTAG extension is unimplemented. The current bit allocation is sufficient for all implemented features.
